predictmeans — notes for Claude Code

Source: CLAUDE.md

R package for predicted means, pairwise comparisons, permutation tests and semiparametric models. Development is toward 2.0; read dev/predictmeans-2.0-plan.md first (aims, decisions, bug list, status table; the row marked “Next” is the current task) and NEWS.md.

Aims (from the maintainer)

  • Statistically right first. Each default is the most reliable method on the evidence (simulation, literature); matching SAS or Genstat is an option the user can choose, not the goal. SAS/Genstat runs check that a formula is computed as documented.
  • Clear logic, not chaos: each statistical decision (df method, covariance, estimability, …) is made in one place and used by every function.
  • Run fast; add emmeans/marginaleffects-style features; keep dependencies few; easy to extend to new model classes (adapter generics in R/adapter.R, see ?pm_coef).

Decisions already made

  • Kenward–Roger adjusted SEs are the default for REML lmer fits; vcov_adjust = FALSE reproduces 1.x numbers.
  • glmmTMB in Imports; car and pbkrtest in Suggests (own code in R/anova.R, R/kr.R, R/satterthwaite.R, R/df-containment.R).
  • Means over empty cells keep the 1.x rule: the average of the observed cells, with a warning (the maintainer’s decision of 2026-11-13, replacing an earlier “NA by default”). Combinations absent by design (nested factors) are not empty cells. Truly non-estimable means are NA.
  • aov models with Error() (aovlist) are analysed by strata, as Genstat: standard errors from the stratum mean squares, never by refitting as lmer. Missing values in an orthogonal design are estimated as Genstat’s ANOVA does (exact SEDs), with a message recommending REML (decision of 2026-11-14).
  • emmeans (and SAS) are not the reference for nested treatment structures or missing combinations (the EOD tree-improvement examples): there predictmeans averages with equal weights over the combinations that exist (tests/testthat/test-nested.R), where emmeans weights by the nesting hierarchy or gives NA.
  • R/inference.R (pm_inference()) decides covariance, df and their labels for every front end; change a df or covariance rule there only.
  • The maintainer can run SAS and Genstat on request: scripts go in dev/sas/ and dev/genstat/. Reference values come only from real runs (uploaded results pages, output or CSV files). Do not use SAS tables typed into chat as references (see dev/sas/README.md).

Layout

  • R/predictmeans.R calls the stages in R/predictmeans-stages.R; the work is done by pure functions there (pm_estimate_means(), pm_compare_*(), pm_make_plots(), …). Only the setup stage edits the call’s state.
  • R/Kmatrix.R + R/refgrid.R: reference grid and K matrix.
  • R/tidy.R, R/autoplot.R: stable means/pairs/settings tables.
  • Help pages: edit the roxygen2 block above each function (data sets in R/data.R, the package page in R/predictmeans-package.R), then Rscript -e 'roxygen2::roxygenise(roclets = "rd")'. NAMESPACE is hand-written — edit it directly.

Checks

  • Tests: NOT_CRAN=true Rscript -e 'devtools::test()' (the 1.1.1 reference tests only run with NOT_CRAN). One file: testthat::test_file(<file>, package = "predictmeans", load_package = "source") (with pkgload::load_all() + test_file() tests can’t see unregistered internal methods). Mixed-model reference values are compared to 2% because lme4/nlme versions move them; everything else to 1e-6.
  • Refactors must not change output: run Rscript dev/snapshot-predictmeans.R <lib> before.rds on the old build and ... after.rds on the new one, then compare with all.equal(readRDS("before.rds"), readRDS("after.rds"), tolerance = 0).
  • Timings: Rscript dev/benchmarks.R.
  • Run R CMD check once at the end of a piece of work, not after every edit.
  • Add a NEWS entry and update the plan’s status table with each change.

Working style the maintainer asked for

  • One step per message; run only the tests related to the change, and R CMD check once at the end.
  • Keep explanations short and plain.
